Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial with much better evidence: the National Revenue Authority's eTax platform (etax.nra.gov.ss) lets taxpayers register, file and pay online, and generated SSP100bn in e-service tax revenue in its first fortnight (Jul 2025), but some agencies (e.g. Civil Aviation Authority) were still resisting adoption as of that date, and immigration/passport fees only went cashless via a bank-linked kiosk in Jan 2026. Coverage is real but not comprehensive across all revenue types, so Partial (2) stands.

Comments: NIPS G2P; govt suppliers via SSIPS ([Global Govt Fintech](https://www.globalgovernmentfinance.com/south-sudan-instant-payments-system-africanenda/)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Limited Use with fresher, more authoritative sourcing. The originally cited 'NIPS' (announced Feb 2025) was largely a design/roadmap document; the system that actually launched as SSIPS on 10 Oct 2025 includes an ACH built for 'bulk, lower-value transactions like salary runs' (Eye Radio, Oct 2025), evidencing early-stage G2P use, but no data exists yet on the share of government disbursements actually digitised — Limited Use remains the accurate code.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed Yes as a design capability: SSIPS, launched 10 Oct 2025, was built to enable real-time transfers between individuals as well as businesses (BoSS Governor, Sudans Post). However, actual P2P usage is constrained since only around 5-6% of adults hold a financial institution account (Global Findex, cited in UNCDF South Sudan report) — capability exists but active uptake is nascent; note this caveat rather than reading 'Yes' as evidence of widespread use.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Constitution Art22 privacy; Cybercrimes Order 2021 user data protection ([Law Gratis](https://www.lawgratis.com/blog-detail/privacy-law-at-south-sudan)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Downgraded from 2 to 1. The original source (a low-authority law blog) mischaracterised the 2021 Cybercrimes Order as data protection legislation. Multiple authoritative, current sources confirm South Sudan has no comprehensive data protection law: the government told parliament it will introduce its first-ever Data Protection Bill only in 2026 (Radio Tamazuj, Dec 2025), and commentary from Feb 2026 confirms the country 'lacks a fully operational, independent Data Protection Act and Authority.' The 2026 Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act addresses cybersecurity, not comprehensive personal data protection. Only the 2011 Transitional Constitution's general privacy clause exists — insufficient for code 2, so the correct code is 1 (No).

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: NPS vision optimal financial inclusion underserved MSMEs ([BoSS NPS](https://boss.gov.ss/national-payment-system/)); no consumer rep mechanisms.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. BoSS's own National Payment System page states a financial-inclusion vision but no explicit consumer/small-provider governance mechanism. A World Bank project document on Strengthening South Sudan's Financial Sector corroborates: the sector 'lacks a harmonized financial consumer protection framework' and a Project Steering Committee (chaired by the BoSS Governor, including private-sector players) is only now being established to guide reform — an inclusion mandate exists in intent, not yet in enforceable governance structures.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial with a stronger corroborating source. A regional displacement/financial-access report ('Displaced and Disconnected') confirms South Sudan has tiered KYC/CDD requirements for mobile money that allow refugees and asylum-seekers to open lowest-tier accounts, with an NGO-issued ID accepted as proof of identity — but formal bank access remains largely excluded, and overall mobile money uptake is low due to weak telecoms infrastructure. This matches 'Partial' rather than 'Yes' (full access) or 'No'.
